advisory.description: phpMyFAQ before 4.1.7 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in SetupController that allows unauthenticated attackers to run database migrations and create configuration backups when maintenance mode is enabled. Attackers can call POST /api/setup/update-database and POST /api/setup/backup endpoints to execute database updates, disable maintenance mode, and extract database credentials from generated ZIP archives.

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: When phpMyFAQ uses PostgreSQL through the native pgsql PHP extension, public FAQ search interpolates the unauthenticated `search` parameter into `Pgsql::search()` as `(%s) ILIKE ('%%%s%%')` after `SearchDatabase::escapeLikeWildcards()`. That helper prefixes user `%` and `_` with `|`, which only disables LIKE wildcards if the SQL also declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Native `Pgsql.php` did not: after the BIC it had no matching ESCAPE clause (PostgreSQL default escape is backslash), and after the later 4.1 merge it declared `ESCAPE '='`. In both states `|` is a literal, so attacker-supplied `%`/`_` stay active wildcards, forcing maximally broad ILIKE matches and expensive sequential scans (availability DoS). Quotes are still passed through `getDb()->escape()`, so this is not quote-breaking SQL injection. The PDO sibling `PdoPgsql.php` declares `ESCAPE '|'` and is not affected.

context_rule: One case, one clean context. Do not read the canonical ledger, another case bundle/output, or a prior verdict. Prior hits are leads, never proof.
